# Nested Classes

**Classes can definitely be nested in C#**. A nested class is a class defined within another class, and it's a powerful feature for organizing related code.


## Basic Syntax


```csharp
public class OuterClass
{
    // Nested class
    public class NestedClass
    {
        public string Message { get; set; }
    }
    
    private int outerField = 10;
    
    public void OuterMethod()
    {
        // Can create instance of nested class
        var nested = new NestedClass();
    }
}

// Usage
var outer = new OuterClass();
var nested = new OuterClass.NestedClass(); // Access via OuterClass
nested.Message = "Hello from nested class";
```


## Access Levels & Scope


Nested classes can have different access modifiers and behaviors:

```csharp
public class DicomStudy
{
    // Public nested class - accessible from outside
    public class Series
    {
        public string SeriesInstanceUID { get; set; }
        public string Modality { get; set; }
    }
    
    // Private nested class - only accessible within DicomStudy
    private class StudyMetadata
    {
        public DateTime StudyDate { get; set; }
        public string ReferringPhysician { get; set; }
    }
    
    // Protected nested class - accessible in derived classes
    protected class StudyStatistics
    {
        public int TotalImages { get; set; }
        public long TotalSizeBytes { get; set; }
    }
}
```


## Key Characteristics


```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│         OuterClass                      │
│  ┌───────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │      NestedClass                  │  │
│  │                                   │  │
│  │  - Can access outer's private     │  │
│  │    members (if non-static)        │  │
│  │                                   │  │
│  │  - Has its own access modifiers   │  │
│  │                                   │  │
│  │  - Full-fledged class             │  │
│  └───────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                                         │
│  - Provides namespace organization      │
│  - Encapsulates related functionality   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```


## Accessing Outer Class Members


A nested class can access private members of the outer class **if it has a reference to an instance**:

```csharp
public class DicomFile
{
    private string _filePath;
    private byte[] _pixelData;
    
    public DicomFile(string path)
    {
        _filePath = path;
    }
    
    // Nested class for metadata extraction
    public class MetadataExtractor
    {
        private DicomFile _parentFile;
        
        public MetadataExtractor(DicomFile parent)
        {
            _parentFile = parent;
        }
        
        public string GetFilePath()
        {
            // Can access private field of outer class through instance
            return _parentFile._filePath;
        }
        
        public bool HasPixelData()
        {
            return _parentFile._pixelData != null;
        }
    }
}

// Usage
var dicomFile = new DicomFile("/path/to/study.dcm");
var extractor = new DicomFile.MetadataExtractor(dicomFile);
string path = extractor.GetFilePath();
```


## Comparison with Python & Dart


**Python:**
```python
class OuterClass:
    class NestedClass:  # Just defines it in the namespace
        def __init__(self):
            self.message = "Hello"
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.field = 10

# Access
nested = OuterClass.NestedClass()  # Similar to C#
```

**Dart:**
```dart
class OuterClass {
  // Dart doesn't support nested classes directly
  // You typically use separate top-level classes
}
```


## When to Use Nested Classes


**Good Use Cases:**

1. **Builder Pattern**
```csharp
public class DicomQuery
{
    public string PatientId { get; private set; }
    public string Modality { get; private set; }
    public DateTime? StudyDateFrom { get; private set; }
    
    private DicomQuery() { }
    
    // Nested Builder class
    public class Builder
    {
        private DicomQuery _query = new DicomQuery();
        
        public Builder WithPatientId(string patientId)
        {
            _query.PatientId = patientId;
            return this;
        }
        
        public Builder WithModality(string modality)
        {
            _query.Modality = modality;
            return this;
        }
        
        public Builder WithStudyDateFrom(DateTime date)
        {
            _query.StudyDateFrom = date;
            return this;
        }
        
        public DicomQuery Build() => _query;
    }
}

// Usage
var query = new DicomQuery.Builder()
    .WithPatientId("12345")
    .WithModality("CT")
    .WithStudyDateFrom(DateTime.Now.AddDays(-30))
    .Build();
```

2. **Tightly Coupled Helper Classes**
```csharp
public class PacsConnection
{
    private string _host;
    private int _port;
    
    // Configuration that only makes sense with PacsConnection
    public class ConnectionConfig
    {
        public int TimeoutSeconds { get; set; } = 30;
        public int MaxRetries { get; set; } = 3;
        public bool UseCompression { get; set; } = true;
    }
}
```

3. **Result/Response Types**
```csharp
public class DicomService
{
    // Nested result class
    public class QueryResult
    {
        public bool Success { get; set; }
        public List<string> StudyInstanceUIDs { get; set; }
        public string ErrorMessage { get; set; }
    }
    
    public QueryResult QueryStudies(string patientId)
    {
        // Implementation
        return new QueryResult { Success = true };
    }
}
```


## When NOT to Use


- **Overly deep nesting** - Makes code hard to navigate
- **When class is used independently** - Just make it a separate class
- **When it bloats the outer class** - Violates single responsibility


## Static Nested Classes


Nested classes can also be static, meaning they don't require an instance of the outer class:

```csharp
public class DicomValidator
{
    // Static nested class - like a utility class
    public static class UidValidator
    {
        public static bool IsValidUid(string uid)
        {
            if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(uid)) return false;
            
            // UID validation logic
            return uid.All(c => char.IsDigit(c) || c == '.');
        }
    }
    
    // Static nested class for constants
    public static class VRCodes
    {
        public const string PersonName = "PN";
        public const string Date = "DA";
        public const string Time = "TM";
        public const string UniqueIdentifier = "UI";
    }
}

// Usage - no instance needed
bool valid = DicomValidator.UidValidator.IsValidUid("1.2.840.113619");
string vrCode = DicomValidator.VRCodes.PersonName;
```


## Summary


| Feature | C# Nested Class |
|---------|----------------|
| **Syntax** | `class Outer { class Nested { } }` |
| **Access** | Via `Outer.Nested` |
| **Can access outer privates** | Yes (with instance reference) |
| **Can be static** | Yes |
| **Access modifiers** | All (public, private, protected, etc.) |
| **Common uses** | Builders, tightly-coupled helpers, result types |


Nested classes are a great organizational tool, but use them judiciously. If your nested class grows large or is needed elsewhere, consider extracting it to a separate file! 🎯
